draft.title: Discrete probability distributions
card: A discrete random variable X takes separate values, such as 0, 1, 2, 3. A probability distribution lists each value x with its probability P(X = x).
Every probability is between 0 and 1. All the probabilities in the table must add to 1, because one of the values must happen.
To find a missing probability, subtract the others from 1. Example: P(1) = 0.3, P(2) = 0.5 and P(3) = k. Then k = 1 − 0.3 − 0.5 = 0.2.
To find the chance of a group of values, add their probabilities. In the example, P(X ≥ 2) = 0.5 + 0.2 = 0.7.
draft.remember: List every value with its probability, and the probabilities add to 1.

a.q: A random variable X has P(1) = 0.2, P(2) = 0.35, P(3) = k and P(4) = 0.25. What is k?
a.why: The probabilities add to 1, so k = 1 − (0.2 + 0.35 + 0.25) = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2. The value 0.8 is the sum of the known probabilities, not the missing one.

b.q: Ava's bus is late X minutes, where P(0) = 0.4, P(5) = 0.3, P(10) = 0.2 and P(15) = 0.1. What is P(X ≥ 5)?
b.why: Add the probabilities for 5, 10 and 15: 0.3 + 0.2 + 0.1 = 0.6. Check: 1 − P(0) = 1 − 0.4 = 0.6. The value 0.9 wrongly leaves out P(0) and counts only part of the rest.
b.clue: At least 5 means 5 or more. Add those probabilities.

problems.detail: Why (b) misdescribes the 0.9 distractor. 0.9 = 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.2, so it wrongly includes P(0) and leaves out P(15). It does not leave out P(0).

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with answers 0.2 and 0.6, and the card is sound. Why (b) wrongly explains the 0.9 distractor: that error comes from including P(0) and leaving out P(15), not from leaving out P(0).

flags: Question b, fact: Why (b) misdescribes the 0.9 distractor. 0.9 = 0.4 + 0.3 + 0.2, so it wrongly includes P(0) and leaves out P(15). It does not leave out P(0).
